attempts.label: DANDI:001474
attempts.paper_title: Obesity dysregulates feeding-evoked response dynamics in hypothalamic satiety neurons
attempts.entry_title: PVH MC4R neuron feeding responses in lean and diet-induced obese mice (Porniece et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Most main findings held in this data, though the neural ones only in direction. HFD mice ate smaller meals and moved less, and NCD mice raised their PVH MC4R response across a meal while HFD mice did not, but exact response sizes matched only under some Z-score readings. The test that HFD early responses exceed NCD did not reproduce (p 0.09 to 0.35), because the paper does not say how the Z-score was computed; the depositors' own Z-score supports it. The diet-switch change in response was not reproduced. The claim that HFD mice needed more training could not be tested, since training sessions are not in the dataset.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Porniece, Baker, Ausfahl, Zhang and Andermann (2025) on dandiset 001474, which holds the fiber photometry of PVH MC4R neurons with licking, running and Ensure delivery in head-fixed NCD and HFD mice during a tone-cued feeding task, in two cohorts and a diet-switch phase. It compares early and late meal responses, licking and meal size between diets, their correlations with body weight, and the effects of fasting and of switching diets.

outcomes.notes: No combination of window (0-10, 1-10, 1-9 s) and Z reading puts all four means within tolerance; Z2 and Z2p put two in. Under Z2 at 0-10 s NCD early is 0.39 against 0.12 +- 0.11, NCD late 1.13 against 0.86 +- 0.09, HFD early 0.72 and HFD late 0.73 against 0.72 and 0.79. NCD late is above NCD early and HFD early above NCD early under every combination. Z1 values are about a third of Z2 (NCD early 0.10 to 0.13, late 0.38 to 0.43). Under Z0 NCD early is -0.17 to -0.23. Cohort 1 holds 38 NCD and 32 HFD recordings with at least 30 triggered trials (6 and 5 mice), against 39 and 33 in the paper. Without the 58 modal-offset recordings at most 2 of 4 means are in tolerance and the partial condition holds in 12 of 12 combinations.
deviations: Z readings Z1 and Z2 (claims file) are computed from the deposited raw 465 nm trace, with trial onsets found from the deposited Z-score; the Methods' "a single Z-score per animal" (Methods, Analysis of head-fixed feeding assays) does not say which recordings are concatenated, so both readings are run, the SD over all the mouse's recordings (Z1, Z2) and over its recordings of one diet phase (Z1p, Z2p).
The depositors' Z-score (Z0) is shown as a variant and does not decide the outcome.
12 trials of two MPK120 recordings in which the raw signal falls to near zero are left out of the raw measures (a standard choice).

outcomes.notes: The criterion's readings disagree. With the pre-tone rate subtracted, late is below early with p < 0.05 in both diets under both AUC windows and both tests (p 0.0001 to 0.031). With division by the pre-tone rate, late is above early in both diets (p 0.31 to 0.78), as the pre-tone lick rate itself falls late in the meal (0.04 to 0.34 licks/s late against 0.13 to 1.05 early). The criterion blocks the claim when the readings disagree. The question of how the AUC was normalized is put to the paper's authors (methods_unavailable finding). deviations: Lick-rate curves in 1-s bins over triggered trials, early and late per recording, averaged per mouse before normalization (a standard choice).

findings.statement: Four files are byte-identical copies of other files of the same subject, deposited under ses-None names (MPK118 2024-02-13, MPK133 2024-02-07, MPK134 2024-02-12, MPK172 2024-07-25, by identifier). Two other ses-None files (MPK122 2024-02-06, MPK143 2024-03-14) are unique sessions whose file names lack the session date.

Cohort 2 holds 6 HFD mice (50 90-trial recordings, 47 with at least 30 triggered trials) where the paper has 7 (54); the missing mouse is a male, by the Supp. Fig. 2k counts. Cohort 1 has 38 and 32 qualifying recordings against 39 and 33, cohort 2 NCD 57 against 59, and the diet-switch first phase 46, 49 and 30 against 47, 52 and 35 for NCD->HFD6w, HFD->NCD and HFD->HFD.
The 405 nm control trace, the training sessions (Supp. Fig. 2q, r) and the home-cage food intake (Fig. 1d) are not in the dataset.

In 32 files the deposited Z-score matrix does not match the raw 465 nm trace of the same file at any offset (median correlation over trials below 0.5), while in the other 285 it does (median 0.95). In 27 files the Z-score (or another series) has more trial columns than the Ensure, lick and running matrices (60 against 59, 90 against 89, and 90 against 60 and 46 in two files).
The starting_time rate of the series is 1 Hz in about half the files (188 of 349 for the Ensure matrix) and 50 Hz in the others; the data are at 50 Hz.

The sex of MPK173 is M in its cohort files and F in its diet-switch files, and that of MPK182 F and M; the cohort-file labels reproduce the paper's female HFD count. The age is P12W/ in every file, for recordings that span a year. One diet-switch file of MPK191 is dated 2024-01-02, before the mouse's cohort recordings of October 2024.

The notes give ensure, bw, ad lib bw and before ad lib bw without units or definitions; which body weight ad lib bw and before ad lib bw are (A and B of Supp. Fig. 3k) has to be guessed. The running signal is signed, with no description of the sign. The session descriptions name a norm_dff series that no file holds. There is no trial table and no tone time stamp; trial onsets in the raw trace have to be inferred.
In two MPK120 recordings (2024-01-25, 2024-01-29) the raw signal falls to near zero in 12 trials, which makes dF/F0 undefined there.

Question for the paper's authors. How was the Z-score computed? Which recordings were concatenated per animal (all, or one diet phase), was it applied to F or to dF/F0, and was each trial's pre-cue baseline subtracted? Under the claims file's two readings (Z1, Z2) the NCD early-meal responses are higher than reported and the Fig. 1k LME does not find HFD early above NCD early (p 0.09 to 0.35), while the depositors' Z-score gives p < 0.001; the deposited Z-score is not a linear transform of the deposited raw trace.

Question for the paper's authors. Supp. Fig. 1d, was the post-cue lick-rate AUC normalized by subtracting or by dividing by the pre-tone lick rate, over which window, and with a paired or unpaired test (the legend and the Methods disagree)? With subtraction licking declines in both diets (p < 0.05); with division it does not.

Question for the paper's authors. Which recordings enter Supp. Fig. 3l-q (at least 30 or at least 15 triggered trials), and what are A and B of Supp. Fig. 3k in the files' notes? The weight-gain correlations of Supp. Fig. 3m are within tolerance only with at least 15 triggered trials.

Supp. Fig. 2h, the text calls the NCD correlation positive and the HFD one negative and prints r = -0.34 and 0.26; the data give the signs of the words (NCD 0.13 to 0.22, HFD -0.003 to -0.33), without significance in both.

The Fig. 3 legend describes recordings with at least 30 of 90 triggered trials, but the diet-switch recordings in the dataset include the 60-trial sessions of the cohort-1 mice in both phases; with them the second-phase counts match the legend for three of the four groups.

entries.name: 001474-porniece-2025
entries.title: PVH MC4R neuron feeding responses in lean and diet-induced obese mice (Porniece et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Porniece, Baker, Ausfahl, Zhang and Andermann (2025) on dandiset 001474, which holds the fiber photometry of PVH MC4R neurons with licking, running and Ensure delivery in head-fixed NCD and HFD mice during a tone-cued feeding task, in two cohorts and a diet-switch phase. It compares early and late meal responses, licking and meal size between diets, their correlations with body weight, and the effects of fasting and of switching diets.
